knowledge:
- key_parameters: id=Gene representation type matching the rownames of the expression data (default is "ENSEMBL") ;; method=Method used to calculate pathway summaries (default is "x2") ;; zNormalize=Logical indicating whether to center and scale pathway summaries across samples (default is TRUE) ;; condition=The covariate column name in the covariates table to contrast (must be formatted as a factor) ;; clusteringFunction=The community detection algorithm used to cluster pathways (e.g., "cluster_louvain") ;; correlationCutOff=The correlation coefficient threshold for filtering edges in the pathway co-expression network ;; sampRate=The number of sampling repeats to empirically obtain the null distribution for miRNA prioritization (recommended between 500-1000) ;; saveSampling=Logical; if TRUE, saves the null distribution sampling to avoid re-running when testing different clustering outputs or thresholds ;; fromID=The input gene ID format for custom enrichment (e.g., "ENSEMBL") ;; toID=The target gene ID format for custom enrichment (e.g., "ENTREZID")
- alternatives: pcxn and pcxnData=Bioconductor packages to access the Pathway Coexpression Network database ;; msigdb=An R package providing a programmatic interface to download different gene set collections, including KEGG and mouse gene sets
- when_to_use: Use this workflow when you have transcriptomics (gene expression) data and want to identify key miRNA regulators that coordinate multiple functionally related pathways, rather than analyzing single miRNA-pathway interactions.
- pitfalls: Ensure that the gene representation type (e.g., ENSEMBL, ENTREZID) matches the rownames of your expression data, otherwise pathway summarization will fail ;; The contrast covariate specified in the condition argument of differentialPathwayAnalysis must be explicitly formatted as a factor ;; Using a low sampling rate (sampRate) in prioritizeMicroRNA can lead to inaccurate empirical p-values; use the recommended 500-1000 range for final analyses ;; KEGG pathways cannot be distributed by third parties due to licensing; users must download them directly from MSigDB in GMT format and import them.

workflows.name: panomir_complete_analysis
workflows.intent: Run the complete PanomiR workflow to identify and prioritize miRNAs targeting coordinated pathway clusters from gene expression data.
input: gene_expression.csv (matrix of gene expression counts/values with genes as rows and samples as columns)
covariates.csv (sample metadata table containing experimental conditions and covariates)
workflows.stages: 1. Summarize pathway activity from gene expression data using pathwaySummary ;; 2. Perform differential pathway activity analysis using differentialPathwayAnalysis ;; 3. Map pathways to clusters using a pathway co-expression network with mappingPathwaysClusters ;; 4. Prioritize miRNAs targeting the pathway clusters using prioritizeMicroRNA
workflows.code:
library(PanomiR)

# Pathway reference from the PanomiR package
data("path_gene_table")
data("miniTestsPanomiR")
# Generating pathway summary statistics 

summaries <- pathwaySummary(miniTestsPanomiR$mini_LIHC_Exp,
                            path_gene_table, method = "x2",
                            zNormalize = TRUE, id = "ENSEMBL")

head(summaries)[,1:2]

output0 <- differentialPathwayAnalysis(
                        geneCounts = miniTestsPanomiR$mini_LIHC_Exp,
                        pathways =  path_gene_table,
                        covariates = miniTestsPanomiR$mini_LIHC_Cov,
                        condition = 'shortLetterCode')

de.paths <- output0$DEP

head(de.paths,3)

# using an updated version of pcxn 

set.seed(2)
pathwayClustsLIHC <- mappingPathwaysClusters(
                            pcxn = miniTestsPanomiR$miniPCXN, 
                            dePathways = de.paths[1:300,],
                            topPathways = 200,
                            outDir=".",
                            plot = FALSE,
                            subplot = FALSE,
                            prefix='',
                            clusteringFunction = "cluster_louvain",
                            correlationCutOff = 0.1)

head(pathwayClustsLIHC$Clustering)

set.seed(1)
output2 <- prioritizeMicroRNA(enriches0 = miniTestsPanomiR$miniEnrich,
                    pathClust = miniTestsPanomiR$miniPathClusts$Clustering,
                    topClust = 1,
                    sampRate = 50, 
                    method = c("aggInv"),
                    outDir = "Output/",
                    dataDir = "outData/",
                    saveSampling = FALSE,
                    runJackKnife = FALSE,
                    numCores = 1,
                    prefix = "outmiR",
                    saveCSV = FALSE)

head(output2$Cluster1)

workflows.name: custom_mirna_pathway_enrichment
workflows.intent: Generate a customized miRNA-pathway enrichment reference table tailored to the user's expressed genes and miRNAs.
input: expressed_genes.txt (list of genes expressed in the experiment)
workflows.stages: 1. Load target scan and MSigDB databases ;; 2. Run Fisher's exact test enrichment using miRNAPathwayEnrichment ;; 3. Generate a simplified publication-ready report using reportEnrichment
workflows.code:
# using an updated version of pcxn
data("msigdb_c2")
data("targetScan_03")


customeTableEnrich <- miRNAPathwayEnrichment(mirSets = targetScan_03,
                                              pathwaySets = msigdb_c2,
                                              geneSelection = yourGenes,
                                              mirSelection = yourMicroRNAs,
                                              fromID = "ENSEMBL",
                                              toID = "ENTREZID",
                                              minPathSize = 9,
                                              numCores = 1,
                                              outDir = ".",
                                              saveOutName = NULL)

workflows.name: custom_pathway_table_from_gmt
workflows.intent: Create a customized pathway-gene association table from an external GMT file or GeneSetCollection.
input: pathways.gmt (external pathway definitions in GMT format)
workflows.stages: 1. Read GMT file into a GeneSetCollection using GSEABase::getGmt ;; 2. Convert the GeneSetCollection to a pathway-gene association table using tableFromGSC
workflows.code:
library(GSEABase)

yourGeneSetCollection <- getGmt("YOUR GMT FILE")
newPathGeneTable      <- tableFromGSC(yourGeneSetCollection)
